blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Customer e-mail address written to the error log on a failed lookup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message — e.g. `throw new NotFoundError("no customer with this e-mail")`. `errorHandler` (src/server.ts) logs `error: err.message` for every failed request, so each lookup of an unknown address writes the typed e-mail (a customer's or a mistyped one) to the application logs, with no purpose and no retention rule (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 5(1)(e)). The same applies to any future message built from personal data.
findings.title: Customer e-mail address written to the error log on a failed lookup

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — the proposal says the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to": the opaque `id` and `name` (and `email` only if the team decides agents need it in the chat). Drop `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` from `chatWidgetSettings`, and select only the needed columns in `customerById`. Sending more to a processor than the purpose needs breaks data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25); these settings are also served to the browser by `GET /chat/settings`, where the widget script can read them.
findings.title: Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The purpose is that agents stop asking customers to repeat who they are; confirm with the team which fields an agent needs to identify the customer, and return only those (likely `id`, `name`, `email`) instead of the whole record, birth date and address included (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Confidence is low: what agents need is not stated in the plan.
findings.title: Support lookup returns the full customer record, birth date and address included

findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the proposal names the chat vendor as a recipient but not whether a processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28) covers Helply, where it stores the data (Chapter V if outside the EEA), how long it keeps chat identities, and how erasure requests reach it. Record these in the plan or the record of processing (Art. 30); the code cannot answer them.
findings.title: Helply is a new processor with no stated agreement or transfer location
